title: I can't code. Claude Code wrote all 66,000 lines of my Roblox roguelite in 4 days.
author: thefillorian
selftext:
I recently moved from Unity to Roblox just to give myself a break from my main project and was really surprised at how well claude code did in the Roblox engine. Especially the spider model and animation. I was also surprised at how fun the end product was. For a long time, I kind of poked fun at Roblox games in a lighthearted way but now found myself playing my game more than I play any other game. Does anyone else use AI to make roblox games? I'd love to have a look at everyone's Roblox projects. Working on this kind of made me imagine a SCI-FI future were nobody really buys games anymore everyone just makes games among their friend groups and each friend group has a special game that only they play and add onto over the years. Eventually making super specialized games with jokes and gameplay that only that group really understands. 

Here's my process: 

I have Claude connected to Roblox studio using the MCP, I've found that the Roblox studio AI access that the MCP grants allow the AI to do a lot more directly in the studio than Unity. I wrote a game design document detailing how I wanted the core and sub gameplay loops to work. Then had a discussion phase with claude and ironed out all the details. Claude can also play the game directly in the studio to playtest features and make sure they are working as intended, but only I can playtest them to determine if they are fun or not. Some things ended up sounding nice mechanically, but not being very fun to play so I axed them. Another interesting thing is that none of the game objects are actually placed in the "scene". Roblox calls them places. Everything is created at runtime via code, even the models and animation. The spider has really cool procedural animation. Only some of the scenery is free roblox creator store models, but even they aren't placed they are spawned in at runtime procedurally. one thing i'm not completely happy with are the sound effects, I'll have to find better ones or make them myself. If anyone has any questions about workflow or process more than happy to answer. 

  
Here is a link if anyone wants to play: [Be a Spider | Play on Roblox](https://www.roblox.com/games/105476179974286/Be-a-Spider)

comments.author: the-liquidian
comments.body: Have you ever seen the number of lines of code written on the cover of a game? Or included in any promotional media, outside of Reddit.

comments.author: thecrownforge
comments.body: The useful part is that you cut mechanics that worked in code but were not fun to play. Did you test the first ten minutes with anyone outside your friend group? I would be curious where they got lost, and whether they wanted a second run without being asked.

replies.author: thefillorian
replies.body: I’ve got analytics set up to see where players leave or give up at any point. However the player count is quite low at the moment as I only went live yesterday. So the data isn’t quite useful yet. I did notice that several people left in the middle of island one and realized I had forgotten something incredibly basic. There was no tutorial. So I quickly made a tutorial that all new players go through the first time they join the game that ends with an easier version of one of the boss fights. Only published that a few hours ago so I’ll see if that was a useful edition soon.
